title: WHAT IF YOU READ A STAR'S FINAL HOURS IN DUST?

segments.line: Hours before this star exploded, its insides got scrambled.
A star is built like an onion, with burning layers.
In its last hours, the carbon and oxygen layers merged.
Then the iron core collapsed and the star blew apart.
The wreckage is Cassiopeia A, eleven thousand light-years away.
Its dust clumps are as big as our solar system.
Webb read that dust, and the chemistry points to the merger.
Silica in one region, carbon in another. Different layers.
NASA says the mixing came very shortly before the blast.
Full film on the channel. Tomorrow: a nuclear reactor on the Moon.
